cars.summary: The S15 Silvia refined Nissan’s compact rear-drive sports-coupe formula through a stronger, more compact body, a new close-ratio six-speed manual, helical differential and revised suspension. The original turbo spec-R is a distinct Silvia generation whose integrated chassis and powertrain development makes it an important Japanese performance-car reference.

cars.variant: Type II — 1990 Japan CA18DET heritage road reference
cars.specification_market: Nissan Heritage Collection No. 323, early 1990 Japan RS13 Type II. Native 175 PS is retained; the English table’s paired 123-kW figure is inconsistent and is excluded without recalculation. CA18DET data do not become later SR20DET/Type X or export KA24 figures. HICAS-II background is not asserted as standard equipment. Export S13 fastbacks are grouped with this identity, not counted as additional badges. Sileighty and pickup/body conversions are excluded.
cars.summary: The 180SX established a long-lived Nissan fastback sports-car identity alongside the Silvia coupe, combining a flowing hatchback body and retractable headlamps with turbo power and multi-link rear suspension. Nissan records its substantial influence on younger drivers and the continuity of its basic design through 1998, supporting its place as a Japanese performance-culture icon.

cars.generation: SR311 original Datsun Sports 2000 open road series
cars.specification_market: Nissan Heritage Collection No. 348 explicitly identifies an early 1967 SR311 for Australia. Its native 107 kW / 145 PS and 176 Nm are not replaced by other-market 135-hp ratings, Solex competition upgrades or restored-car claims. Maximum-speed superlative, acceleration, gearbox and exact carburettor specification are omitted. This roadster is distinct from the Fairlady Z coupe and existing CSP311 Silvia, despite historical shared components.
cars.summary: The SR311 Fairlady, exported as Datsun 2000 Sports, is a defining development of Nissan’s traditional open sports car. Its compact roadster body and U20 overhead-cam two-litre engine brought substantial performance to the marque’s international sports-car identity, with the preserved early Australian example documenting that export history.

cars.variant: 370Z — 2009 US six-speed manual with Sport Package
cars.specification_market: November 19, 2008 US press kit, original 2009 370Z coupe sections. Selected manual with optional Sport Package; rev matching and viscous LSD are not claimed for the base package. US native hp/lb-ft remain unconverted. NISMO 350-hp engine/chassis, seven-speed automatic, adjacent 350Z Roadster content and later facelift/anniversary data are excluded. No claim that the exterior photograph authenticates this transmission/package or exact body-panel material.
cars.summary: The Z34 370Z substantially reworked Nissan’s Z sports coupe with a shorter wheelbase, lighter body materials and the VVEL-equipped VQ37VHR engine. Its optional Sport Package introduced SynchroRev Match to the manual transmission, a notable road-car control innovation that retained the driver-operated clutch and gear lever within the continuing Z lineage.
